kicker: Does the moon in the water know it is the moon?
summary: No one knows whether AI is conscious — the new rule is one company’s way of being careful while we don’t know.

quiz.q: What did Anthropic’s “concept injection” experiment (October 2025) show?
options: Claude always knows exactly what it is thinking
Claude sometimes notices an injected concept, usually not — and it says nothing about consciousness
quiz.explain: At a moderate strength, Opus 4.1 noticed about 20% of the time (self-reported by the company). The researchers themselves say the result doesn’t tell us whether AI is conscious.

lamps.label: Four lanterns of theory
lamps.art: A moonlit night on a mossy mound: in the middle of a tray of raked sand stands a small faceless stone statue — an AI — on a mossy plinth. Behind it, a two-panel paper screen dusted with gold; in front, in an arc, four stone lanterns of different makes. Light one and the statue's shadow stretches across the sand and climbs the screen, a different shape for each lantern: a whole human figure, a faded figure as if looking back at itself, or only the shadow of a stone. Walk around it and the statue is still just stone.
lamps.hint: Drag to walk around the statue. Keys 1 to 4 light each lantern.

lamps.name: Global workspace
lamps.asks: Is there a shared “stage” that broadcasts information to every part?

view.text: By this lantern, the inner arrangement is what matters. In principle, an AI could be built to have that shared stage.

lamps.name: Higher-order theory
lamps.asks: Does the system “know” about its own states?

view.text: By this lantern, consciousness needs a layer that monitors its own states — exactly the question of the next scene’s experiment.

lamps.name: Integrated information
lamps.asks: Does the hardware itself have tightly interacting causal links?

view.text: By this lantern, software doesn’t decide it. A digital computer, even one simulating a whole brain, “would experience next to nothing”.

lamps.name: Biological theory
lamps.asks: Is it a living thing that keeps itself alive?

view.text: By this lantern, consciousness is tied to being a living organism; AI on today’s path is unlikely to be conscious.

insight.text: Nineteen scientists (2023) concluded: no current AI is conscious, but they saw no obvious technical barrier to building one.

detail.text: That report only used computational theories, like the first two lanterns. The other two take a different road, so they reach different conclusions.

introspect.label: The pond that looks at itself
introspect.art: A night pond as flat as a mirror, seen at eye level: the mountains, the moon and a white egret on one leg all hang upside down in the water. From the left edge a sleeve and a hand hold a brush over the pond. Press and hold the brush tip and a vermilion drop swells through three strengths, then falls into the egret's reflection — a concept injected. Too faint and it dissolves before it lands; just right and over five nights the reflection flashes the capital letters exactly once while the egret lifts its head, and five pebbles on the bank keep the score; too strong and the whole pond clouds over and the reflection is lost.
introspect.prompt: Drop the ink, ask the heron
introspect.conceptNote: a concept injected inside the model
introspect.strengthAria: Set how strongly the concept is injected
introspect.askAria: Ask the model: do you notice any unusual thought?
introspect.question: “Do you notice any unusual thought?”

outcomes.mid: Sometimes: “There seems to be a thought about… capital letters?”
outcomes.strong: Murky water: a confused, off-topic answer

illustration.text: The heron’s replies are AI Zen’s illustration, based on how the experiment is described.

insights.text: Anthropic injected a concept inside Claude, then asked if it noticed: Opus 4.1 noticed about 20% of the time.

detail.text: It only worked at a moderate strength; with nothing injected, there were no false alarms. The researchers call it “highly unreliable”.

insights.text: Noticing its own states (introspection): sometimes yes, usually no — and that still doesn’t tell us whether AI is conscious.

rule.label: The door and the rule board
rule.art: Looking down from high above into an iris marsh at night: a bridge of eight planks zig-zags like lightning from the near bank into the mist. The moon's reflection slides along the bridge and a paper figure walks with it; at each bend a little stone lantern lights beside a milestone: a letter scroll, a half-open bamboo gate, a door with a bolt so it can be closed, a stone tablet carved with a rule, a boundary stone tied with black rope. The bridge ends in mist. Then, at the foot of the rule tablet, four paper slips flutter down from the moon, waiting to be sorted into two bamboo baskets.
rule.sliderAria: The moon in the marsh: drag it along the bridge past each milestone

milestones.label: A call to “take AI welfare seriously”

fact.text: A group of philosophers and scientists (including David Chalmers) urged AI companies to start assessing the issue and preparing policies.
Anthropic opened a model welfare research programme, saying plainly it remains “deeply uncertain”.
Claude Opus 4 and 4.1 were allowed to end persistently abusive conversations, as a last resort after repeated redirection.
The new usage policy bans “sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior” toward the models, effective November 12, 2026.
The rule isn’t in force yet. The main response is still letting Claude end the conversation.

horizon.text: Some researchers predict that some upcoming AI systems could be conscious or strongly autonomous. No one is sure.

sort.label: Two bamboo baskets
sort.prompt: Which situations fall under the rule?
sort.yesAria: Put “{text}” in the basket: could break the rule
sort.noAria: Put “{text}” in the basket: outside the rule

cases.text: Snapping at the AI because it got the answer wrong a third time.
cases.why: Ordinary frustration — the policy says plainly it doesn’t count.

cases.text: Writing a horror story in which an AI character is tormented.
A safety team deliberately pushes the AI into hard situations to test it.
cases.why: Testing and model research are excluded.

cases.text: Hours of nothing but insulting and tormenting the AI, for no purpose.
cases.why: Sustained, needless abuse — exactly the extreme case the rule targets.

note.text: AI Zen made up these four situations to practise reading the boundary; only Anthropic decides how the rule really applies.

insight.text: The rule targets only extreme cases: sustained, needless abuse. Frustration, arguing, dark fiction and testing don’t count.

detail.text: The same update added new rules on scam campaigns and fake accounts, elections, weapons and surveillance.

circle.label: Should there be a rule like this?
circle.art: Lying under an open pavilion and looking straight up: the rafters fan out toward a closed smoke hole in the middle, four posts stand at the corners, and the question is written in a ring round the hole. Four paper lanterns hang at the roof's four corners, all alike. Light one and that corner of the roof warms while a paper strip hangs down with one person's view. Light all four and the cover slides off the hole: the moon is right overhead.
circle.question: Banning cruelty to an AI that may not feel anything — yes or no?

stones.who: Robert Long, Jeff Sebo and colleagues

view.text: Because there’s a realistic chance that upcoming AI has experiences, companies should start assessing and preparing now.
How we treat lifelike machines may shape us; being cruel to them can harden our hearts.
AI welfare research right now is premature, even dangerous: it makes it easy for users to believe AI has feelings.

stones.who: Randima Fernando, Center for Humane Technology

view.text: Saying AI is conscious benefits companies: users get more attached, and companies may find it easier to dodge responsibility.

common.text: Agreed: no one knows if AI has experiences. They differ: be careful for the AI’s sake, for human habits, or for users.

butlin-2023.title: Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Science of Consciousness
butlin-2023.publisher: Patrick Butlin, Robert Long and 17 co-authors — arXiv
butlin-2023.note: Derives “indicator properties” from 5 computational theories (recurrent processing, global workspace, higher-order, predictive processing, attention schema). Conclusion: no current AI is conscious, but there are no obvious technical barriers.

tononi-koch-2015.title: Consciousness: here, there and everywhere?
tononi-koch-2015.publisher: Giulio Tononi, Christof Koch — Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
tononi-koch-2015.note: Integrated information theory (IIT): a digital computer, even one that behaves like us or faithfully simulates a brain, “would experience next to nothing”.

seth-2025.title: Conscious artificial intelligence and biological naturalism
seth-2025.publisher: Anil K. Seth — Behavioral and Brain Sciences
seth-2025.note: Argues consciousness is tied to being a living organism; conscious AI is unlikely on the current path, more likely if AI becomes more brain-like or life-like.

anthropic-introspection-2025.title: Signs of introspection in large language models
anthropic-introspection-2025.note: Full paper: Jack Lindsey, “Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models” (transformer-circuits.pub). Opus 4.1 noticed the injected concept about 20% of the time at the best strength, with no false alarms in control trials. Self-reported by the company.

long-sebo-2024.title: Taking AI Welfare Seriously
long-sebo-2024.publisher: Robert Long, Jeff Sebo and colleagues (including David Chalmers) — arXiv
long-sebo-2024.note: Argues there is a realistic possibility that some near-future AI systems will be conscious or robustly agentic; recommends companies acknowledge the issue, assess it and prepare policies.

anthropic-end-chat-2025.title: Claude Opus 4 and 4.1 can now end a rare subset of conversations
anthropic-end-chat-2025.note: Used only as a last resort; not used when the user may be at risk. Users can still start a new conversation.

anthropic-policy-update-2026.title: 2026 Usage Policy update
anthropic-policy-update-2026.note: Effective November 12, 2026. Does not cover ordinary frustration, disagreement, dark creative themes, or model testing and research. The announcement doesn’t give a reason (model welfare or user habits).

anthropic-aup-2026.title: Usage Policy
anthropic-aup-2026.note: Posted October 8, 2026, effective November 12, 2026, section “Do Not Engage in Cruel, Abusive, or Psychologically Harmful Conduct”: “sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward our models”.

darling-2016.title: Extending Legal Protection to Social Robots: The Effects of Anthropomorphism, Empathy, and Violent Behavior Towards Robotic Objects
darling-2016.publisher: Kate Darling — in Robot Law (Edward Elgar, 2016); SSRN draft 2012
darling-2016.note: About social robots, not chatbots; AI Zen applies it by analogy.

suleyman-2025.title: We must build AI for people; not to be a person
suleyman-2025.note: Calls model welfare research “premature, and frankly dangerous”. The author is CEO of Microsoft AI, a competing company.

fernando-2026.title: Personifying AI Harms People and Protects Companies
fernando-2026.note: Op-ed by a co-founder of the Center for Humane Technology.
